title: Harder 328: the vote narrows the gap to RL, not closes it
what: Each model answered the 328 harder problems four times, again after a cut-off answer; the most common answer was graded. Base with cue 195 of 328, RL 224. RL minus base 8.8 points [5.5, 12.5]; one sample: 14.0.
why: The procedure was fixed on MATH-500 and nothing was chosen on the 328, so this is the held-out reading of the vote result. RL stays ahead under every rule tried.
caveat: The shortest-answer tie-break does not hold up here (191 against the vote's 192), so its 453 on MATH-500 was chosen in-sample; quote the plain vote.

Predictions (spec DAY1_hard328_vote): 1, 2, 4 hold (RL vote 221, base vote 192, gap 8.8). Refuted: 3 (restarts add 0.9 points to the vote, not 2.0), 5 (tie_short -0.3 [-2.1, 1.5]), 6 on tokens (stop-when-two-agree keeps the score, saves 7 %, not 20 %). Seeds differ by up to 9 (base) and 19 (RL) problems per sample.
Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/, hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/, results/selector/hard328_base_cue-01/, results/frontier/hard328-01/frontier.md; README section 'The 328 with four samples and restarts'; jobs e8e6, 5ff2.

The RL gain is not practice on its training prompts: D = (RL - Code-RL) seen minus unseen = +2.9 points, 95 % interval [-4.8, +10.6], per sample (vote over 4: +4.9 [-7.3, 17.2]); D >= +15 refuted, up to ~10 not excluded. 72 harder problems in the RL training prompts (43 exact, 29 near) against 130 source-matched unseen, 4 samples, T 1.0, v3. Per sample right seen / unseen: base+cue 20.8 / 40.0, RL 37.5 / 55.5, Code-RL cue 30.6 / 51.4, Think-SFT cue 46.2 / 62.0 percent. Seen problems are 19 points harder for the base ([-28.7, -9.2]), not easier: no pretraining-exposure benefit; the Dolci filter kept prompts the base fails. With base as control D = +1.2 [-6.4, 8.8]; exact +3.3, near +2.3 (Code-RL). RL answers on seen problems are worked (shortest right one 2,574 tokens; median 9,346 vs 6,802 on unseen AIME). Code-RL card: code-only RL data, valid control. Year not matched. No score line: the 72 are not a chart benchmark. studies/rlneurons/results/seen/readout.json, README section 'Seen against unseen' (main 2cb64e0).

title: RL's directions lengthen short answers and cut the tail
what: From stored rows of the edit cells on 328 hard problems: answer lengths against the base on problems both finish, right answers within a token budget, and a restart of unfinished problems with the twice-size edit.
why: Not known yet.
caveat: Truncating a stored run at C estimates a cap-C run. One sample per cell. The cascade spends 26% more tokens than RL alone.
Lengths base -> cell (p10/p50/p90 tokens): top-8 1252/5513/14398 -> 1654/6094/14816; 2x 1297/6409/14487 -> 2107/7088/12308; RL 1295/6174/13532 -> 2401/7718/13532; random rank-8 ratio 1.00. Predicted 'median within 10%, only tail falls': refuted, p10 rises 32-72%. Budget 4k tokens: base 81 right, top-64 66, RL 69; base leads below 4k. Cascade top-64 cut at 14k then 2x restart: 207/328 at 11,696 tokens (RL 206 at 9,316; +0.3 pts [-3.4, 4.0]); restart with the random-edit cell 198. Branch sharedsub, studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/lengths-01/readout.json, analysis/xreward_lengths.py. work-e02ba4.
score: other hard328 207/328 tokens 11696 | base + 64 directions cut at 14k tokens, unfinished restart with 8 directions at 2x; cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0

On the 328 the base-to-RL gap is not a selection problem. Vote over 4: RL right and base wrong on 36 problems; the base has a right sample among its four on only 10 of them, none on 26. A perfect selector over the base's four samples (pass@4 = 207) only equals one RL sample (207); the base's vote loses 15 problems to selection, RL's 19. Base-only wins: 7. Neither model: 100 under the vote, 79 with any right sample after restarts. So better voting or tie rules cannot close the gap here; it needs answers the base never writes (weights or longer reasoning: see Think-SFT, cap 32,768). Source: per_problem in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/readout.json and hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/readout.json (result-5c961a).

title: Lowering the base's wrong steps adds no right answers
what: From the token before 51 wrong steps of the cued base, 306 continuations per arm: plain base 99 right, problem contrast 104 (+1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8]), RL continuing the base text 132 (+10.8 [5.6, 16.3]).
why: The rule lowered the wrong steps by 1.69 nats in the screen but does not fix answers in generation, so no MATH-500 cell with it.
caveat: 55 % of rows hit the 4,000-token cap; RL's gain is all in capped rows (42 scored right on a box inside the reasoning, base 9). Ended rows: RL 90, base 90.
Details: T 1.0, grader v3. Contrast = softmax(2 logits - logits without the problem). Misreadings 27 to 36 of 84 (+10.7 [-1.2, 22.6]); slips, wrong plans unchanged. studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/prefix-01/, README 'Wrong steps', on main b443163.

title: Mixing RL and Think-SFT samples in one vote does not help
what: On the 328 harder problems a vote over two RL and two Think-SFT samples scores 228.1, between four RL samples (221) and four Think-SFT samples (241). All eight samples together score 239.
why: Think-SFT, trained with no reward, is right on 26 problems where RL's vote is wrong and RL on only 6, so RL samples dilute the vote. Four Think-SFT samples are the best row on the 328 so far.
caveat: Stored rows, no new generation. Think-SFT's score line belongs to work-0a00c2, so none is posted here. 6 of the 328 match Think-SFT training prompts; the lead holds without them.
Think-SFT minus RL: +2.7 pts [0.4, 5.2] on one sample (209.0 vs 200.0, four samples each), +6.1 [3.0, 9.5] under vote over 4 (241 vs 221; 40,410 vs 37,299 tokens per problem). 2 RL + 2 Think-SFT minus 4 Think-SFT: -3.9 [-6.2, -1.8]. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/mixvote/hard328-01/readout.json, analysis/mixvote.py, README section 'Mixed-model vote on the 328' (main 37be2ce).

Think-SFT + cue (no reward, trained on traces) beats RL under the vote on the 328: vote over 4 = 241/328 at 40,410 tok vs RL plain 221 (224 after restart) and base+cue 192: +6.1 pts [3.0, 9.5] paired; sequential vote (chosen on MATH-500) 241 (238.9 over 24 orders) at 30,904 tok vs RL 224 (218.2) at 31,326. Singles 212/212/211/201 (mean 209.0) vs RL 207/190/209/194 (200.0): +2.7 [0.4, 5.2]. MATH-500 n=500: vote 481 at 19,503 tok vs RL 474 (+1.4 [-0.4, 3.2], not separated), sequential 481 at 11,521; singles 457-462. T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, 4 samples, no restarts for Think-SFT. Instrument: hard328 sample 0 = 212 with 89 cap hits (sameraslan 219, 89); MATH-500 sample 0 = 461 (stored 454). Without the training-prompt matches of result-f6a8bc: hard328 n=322 vote 235 vs RL 215; MATH-500 n=475 456 vs 450. Predictions: MATH-500 vote 481 is outside the filed 473.1 [466,480] (Rasch) and 472.1 [464,480] (hazard) and above the 479 that refutes the one-axis claim (both rules started from single 454; measured 457-462). hard328 vote: Rasch 238.6/243.8, mine 238 [228,250] held, point rules 234/245.9; Rasch nearest, all within noise. hard328 single mean 209.0: profile_corrected 209.2 wins, Lc 196.3. Why (raw rows): Think-SFT abstains instead of answering wrong: 29 % cap hits on the 328 (RL 9 %), finished answers right 88.0 % (RL 66.2 %), so its vote is almost pass@4 (241 vs 244; RL 221 vs 240). Cap hits are unfinished reasoning, not loops (rule A 6 of 378; 86 switch into Chinese). On MATH-500 16 of its 74 finished wrong answers end in a line equal to the gold (answer on the line after 'Answer:'; RL 0 of 131): v3 undercounts it by ~4 per sample. Not controlled: responses in the training set unscanned; RL/base rows have restarts. Stack (Part B) not run: work-3d1e3b. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/ (hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01, math500_sft1_cue_s4-01, frontier_*-01, scored-01), README 'Think-SFT with the cue under the vote rules', main c0dd7c4.

title: A slip is chance; a misreading starts before its sentence
what: From the token before a slip the base is right as often as from the start of the problem (49.2 % vs 47.6 %, 21 prefixes); before a judged misreading it has already lost 32 points (32.1 % vs 64.3 %, 14 prefixes).
why: Slips fit a per-step chance of error, so resampling helps them; misreadings are set up earlier in the text than the sentence the judge quoted.
caveat: 51 prefixes, 6 continuations each, cap 4,000 new tokens; from-scratch rate counts the other 3 stored samples within the same token budget.
Differences: slip +1.6 points [-11.9, 14.3], misread -32.1 [-50.0, -16.7], wrong plan -6.2 [-19.8, 5.2], all -10.1 [-19.6, -1.6]. studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/prefix_vs_scratch-01/metrics.json, analysis/prefix_vs_scratch.py, README 'Wrong steps'. Follows result-a497ff.

title: How much the early text depends on the problem tells nothing
what: For the base's 2,000 stored samples, log p(token | problem) - log p(token | no problem) over the first 1,000 tokens ranks the right sample above the wrong one of the same problem in 53.1 % of pairs [46.8, 58.9]; chance is 50.
why: A third label-free early signal fails (after activations 57.1 and the base's own likelihood 51.9), so stopping bad samples early has no working detector; answer length (68.0) is known only at the end.
caveat: 150 problems with both outcomes, 478 pairs. The lowest tenth of the token values reaches 57.5 [51.6, 63.7], the same as the activation probe.
Predictions P1 and P3 refuted: misread samples do not have the lowest value (0.132 nats per token; slip 0.094, wrong plan 0.154). studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/probdep-01/, specs/SPEC_probdep.md, README 'Wrong steps'. One 10-minute A100 job on vast.ai.

Closed routes for 'catch or avoid a wrong base sample while it is being written, no label, no second model' (cued base, MATH-500, all on main, studies/rlneurons README 'Critic at decoding time' and 'Wrong steps'). Early detectors, within-problem AUROC right vs wrong at 1,000 tokens: linear probe on activations 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] (result-b30f15); base's own mean log p 0.519; problem dependence log p(tok|problem) - log p(tok|no problem) 0.531 [0.468, 0.589] (result-f3d708); RL's likelihood of the base text is length only (0.853 vs 0.855). Bound: a perfect detector at 1,000 tokens gives 438.7/500 against 410.5, so even a working one stays below the vote (446). Steering: problem contrast (context-aware decoding) from before the wrong step +1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8], gains above 8 excluded (result-a497ff); T 0.6 raises the wrong steps. What did hold: Math-RL is half as likely to write the base's wrong step (D -0.71 nats); a misreading has cost 32 points before its sentence (result-c495fe); RL capped rows already hold a boxed answer in 69 % of cases, base capped rows in 17 %. Not tested: detectors trained across problems on more data; contrast from the first answer token on a full cell (expected gain under 2 points, below what n 500 resolves).

Null: no two-model relay beats Think-SFT finishing its own answer on hard328 (n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample). Best relay, Think-SFT writes the first 50 % and RL-Zero-Math finishes: 209/328 at 8,923 tokens per problem, vs its control Think->Think 211 (-0.6 pts [-4.3, +3.0]), the stored Think-SFT sample 212 at 10,140 (219 in the other workspace) and RL 206 at 9,315. At 25 %: 207 vs control 219 (-3.7 [-7.6, +0.3]). RL->Think 204 / 199 vs RL->RL 206 / 193. On Think-SFT's 89 cap-hit prefixes RL as finisher has 18 and 17 right, Think 18 and 16: RL ends the cap hits (13 for 96 over the 328) but 59 to 65 of the 89 become wrong boxed answers. Only gain: Think finishing RL's 102 finished-wrong answers at 50 %: 10 vs 4 (+5.9 [1.0, 10.8]), paid with 71 cap hits. Predictions filed first (141c605): H1 refuted as predicted, 6 of 8 arm scores inside the filed ranges. Jobs 6d5e 3d3b 6338 d35a, 5.6 H100-h. title: Handing a Think-SFT answer to RL to finish gains nothing
what: One model wrote the first 25 or 50 % of an answer on the 328 harder problems and the other finished it, for both orders, against each model finishing its own answer.
why: RL stops where Think-SFT would run out of tokens, but it stops on a wrong answer: on the 89 cap-hit prefixes both finishers get 16 to 18 right.
caveat: One sample per prefix; RL finishing its own 50 % prefix scored 193 against 206 stored, so arms are compared with the own-prefix controls.

Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 is in long answers only. Keeping each model's shortest answers, precision is equal up to coverage 0.50 (94.8 % vs 93.0 %, +1.8 points [-0.8, +5.5]) and Think-SFT leads by +8.8 [6.4, 12.5] at 0.75 (n 328, 1,312 samples each, attempt 0, T 1.0, v3; base 82.3 % and 63.9 %). Finished answers over 12,000 tokens: right 68.2 % Think-SFT (135/198), 24.4 % RL (87/356), 16.7 % base (41/246); under 12,000 tokens RL has more right samples (706 vs 687). MATH-500: no lead at any coverage. Where a Think-SFT sample gives no answer, RL's is wrong 248 times, right 52. RL's precision on the 141 problems with a Think-SFT cap hit is 31.2 %, against 35.2 % expected from the base's solve rate: mostly difficulty (-3.9 [-6.9, -1.0]). Dropping samples longer than L before the vote (L from MATH-500) does not help: RL 224 vs 221 (+0.9 [0.0, 2.1]), base 189 vs 192. Hand read of 10 long wrong RL answers: 6 box a number the write-up does not derive. Vote check 241/221/192 reproduced. studies/rlneurons/results/riskcov/hard328-01/readout.json, table.md; README section 'Risk-coverage'

title: One cell can now run as N jobs at once
what: run_cell --shard k/N runs problems k, k+N, ... of a set; analysis/shard_join.py joins the N run folders into the folder one job would have written (main 329dd7b, studies/rlneurons/README.md section 'One cell on N GPUs').
why: on a 48 GB GPU the long answers fill the KV cache, 9-12 sequences run and the rest wait (about 200 tokens/s, job ih-1115-092337-b35c: 110 of 500 answers in 23 min). N small GPUs each have their own cache.
Checks: real 2-shard run on two L40S, MATH-500 --n 24: 24 problems, each once, every seed = seed + index, 18 right; laptop dry run, 3 shards = the unsharded run's 22 requests, seeds and prompts; shard_join_test, 7 planted cases (5 must fail).
caveat: not compared row by row with an unsharded GPU run; batch composition differs, so texts can differ as between any two runs. Use: add --shard 0/4 .. 3/4 to the same command, then shard_join --runs <4 folders> --out <name>.

title: Think-SFT's lead on the 328 survives a full data scan
what: All 156 shards and every turn (user and response) of Think-SFT's training set were compared with the test problems. The same 6 of the 328 harder problems match as before; none are new. Without them Think-SFT's vote is 235 of 322, RL's 215.
why: The claim that a model trained with no reward beats RL on the 328 needed the test problems to be absent from its training text. This closes the open part of that check: +6.2 points [3.1, 9.6] without the 6, +6.1 with them.
caveat: The rule finds copies of the text (exact, or half of the 8-word runs). Paraphrases, translations and versions with changed numbers are not detected; the fresh post-cutoff set (work-7c069c) covers that.
2,268,178 rows, 36.1 GB, allenai/Dolci-Think-SFT-7B @83f618e. MATH-500: 29 flagged (25 in user turns as before; 4 new only in responses: 289, 406, 438, 439, phrases inside other problems' reasoning, not copies). Planted-copy selftest passes (user, respaced, response copy found; 40 % copy not flagged). Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/wsp1/sft_overlap-03/ (metrics.json, flags.json, selftest.txt), analysis/wsp1_sft_overlap.py --turns all, README section.

title: The base reaches the cue's score with no cue prefilled
what: On MATH-500 the untrained base drew up to 32 openings of 24 tokens per problem at T 1.0 and continued the first one that opens with a newline then 'Okay'; nothing was prefilled.
why: Choosing among the base's own first tokens gives the whole gain of the opening cue, so the cue adds no information the base does not already produce.
caveat: One sample per problem; shards ran on two GPU types; 94 problems keep their stored plain answer, which already opened this way.

RL did not add the habit of boxing an underived number: among long (>8,000 tokens) finished wrong hard328 answers a blind judge labels 72.5 % of RL's as asserted [63.1, 81.3], 66.2 % of the cued base's [54.6, 77.2] and 36.2 % of Think-SFT's [24.4, 48.6] (80 rows each). RL minus base +6.2 points [-6.7, 19.1] (H1 refuted); RL minus Think-SFT +36.2 [23.3, 49.1]. H2 held: RL's asserted long answers are right 17.0 % [9.0, 25.6] of the time, derived ones 66.1 % [56.5, 75.2]. H3 not held: dropping the 319 RL answers a second judge flags gives precision 78.0 % at coverage 72.9 % against 77.4 % for keeping the shortest answers, +0.5 points [-1.4, 2.6]. Instrument: planted controls 15/15 and 15/15; kappa of two judge models 0.80 (420 rows); kappa against 30 blind labels by the agent 0.60, at the bar (judge 11 asserted, hand 6: the judge's label includes answers resting on a conjecture); tail against full text 38/40. Judge claude-sonnet-5-5 (sees the problem and the last 3,000 tokens, not the model, gold or score), second judge claude-haiku-5-5; 7.37 USD. No Exa key: WebSearch only, no paper read. Artifact: studies/rlneurons/results/derived/hard328-01/ (readout.json, table.md, labels.jsonl, hand.json, examples.json); spec studies/rlneurons/specs/SPEC_derived.md at a9b65ed; main 92e6e1d.
title: Unsolved long answers guess: the base as often as RL
what: A blind judge read the end of long wrong answers. RL states its final number without deriving it in 72.5 % of them, the untrained base in 66.2 %, Think-SFT in 36.2 % (80 answers each, harder set).
why: The reward did not create the guessing: the base does it as often. Think-SFT differs; it mostly keeps working until the token cap. Flagging guesses helps no more than cutting long answers.
caveat: The judge is a model; its agreement with 30 blind labels by the agent is at the bar (kappa 0.60), and it calls an answer asserted more often than that read does.

Correction of result-b006f5: Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 is in long answers to hard problems; both matter (n 328, 4 samples each, stored rows). Reviewer's numbers reproduce: 81.1 % / 80.6 % of samples kept at coverage 0.50 are from the 149 problems the cued base solves 3-4 of 4 (both 98.5 % right); on the other 179 Think-SFT leads at coverage 0.30 by +15.8 points [7.4, 25.6], but that point is at 12,715 / 11,161 tokens. Difficulty held (base right 1-2 of 4): lead +29.1 [19.1, 39.4] in finished answers over 8,000 tokens, +4.4 [-3.8, 14.1] under; long minus short +24.8 [10.5, 38.4]. Length held (over 8,000 tokens): +34.5 [24.9, 43.7] where the base is never right, +29.1 at 1-2, +6.8 [-0.6, 13.4] at 3-4. Problem held (problem x model fixed effects): an RL answer over 8,000 tokens is right 12.5 points less often than its shorter answers to the same problem [-20.8, -4.8], Think-SFT's +1.2 [-4.0, 7.0]; difference +13.7 [3.9, 23.8]. Leave-one-out stratifier without the base agrees on length (4-6 of 6: +18.2 [12.8, 23.7] long, +0.4 [-1.0, 1.8] short). The 28 problems with a short and a long answer from both models: +10.3 [-3.7, 25.0]. studies/rlneurons/results/riskcov/hard328_strat-01/ (readout.json, table.md, examples.json), analysis/riskcov_strat.py, specs/SPEC_riskcov.md addendum 1, README section 'Risk-coverage' (commit 0a7de7c).
title: Think-SFT's lead: long answers to hard problems
what: Corrects an earlier result. The supervised model beats the reward-trained one only on long answers (over 8,000 tokens), and mostly on problems the untrained model rarely solves. Short answers are equally reliable.
why: The first claim said long answers only; a review said hard problems, not long answers. Tests fixed in advance refute both: the lead needs length and difficulty together.
caveat: Hard problems almost never get short answers (11 and 18 samples), so that case is untested. Difficulty is measured from 4 samples of the untrained model.

Loop-neuron edit over four samples per problem (base+cue, MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 1.0, v3, attempt 0 of run_cell --samples 4): it does add right answers at T 0.6. The unedited job stopped at its 4 h limit after all first attempts. title: One table of every configuration on the 328 harder problems
what: Rebuilt all 49 full-set configurations on the 328 from committed per-problem rows, with one definition of the share of the base-to-RL gap closed and a check of each posted number.
why: Think-SFT with the cue, which uses no reward, closes 122 % [103, 144] of the gap at one sample and 169 % [128, 250] under the vote. The untrained base's best rules close 20 % [13, 29] and 24 % [0, 50].
caveat: The vote's gap is 29 problems, so vote shares have wide intervals. Think-SFT is trained on traces. Left out for lack of committed rows: weight stack and cap 32k (both open), top-k RL directions, loop-neuron edit.
Numbers (hard328, n 328, T 1.0, v3, nothing chosen on the 328): Think-SFT + cue one sample 209.0 vs RL 200.0 and cued base 158.5; vote over 4 241 vs 221 and 192. Base: restart 167.0 at one sample; vote after restart with ties to the shortest 199.
At the tokens of one RL sample (9,325): one Think-SFT sample costs 1.08x [1.06, 1.11]; stopped at 14,028 tokens it costs 1.00x and closes 79 % [62, 98], 2.7 points [0.2, 5.1] below one RL sample and level with RL stopped at the same length (+0.1 [-2.2, 2.4]); the untrained base at that budget is 0 %.
Unexplained: the 12.7 points [10.1, 15.5] between one cued-base and one RL sample (8.8 [5.2, 12.8] under the vote) are reached by no rule on untrained weights; Think-SFT's lead over RL is 17.8 right answers per sample longer than 14,028 tokens (5.4 points [4.0, 6.9]); whether RL stops too early there is untested (work-ceccc0).

title: Per attempt, RL guesses more often than the base
what: Counting every attempt on the harder set, RL ends with a long wrong answer whose final number is not derived in 21.1 % of attempts, the untrained base in 14.2 %, Think-SFT in 2.7 % (1,312 attempts each).
why: The earlier headline 'RL did not add the habit' was too strong. When RL finishes long and wrong it guesses as often as the base, but it finishes far more often: the base runs out of tokens on 286 attempts, RL on 114.
caveat: The judge is a model. The base's and Think-SFT's rates rest on 80 judged answers each, scaled up; answers under 8,000 tokens were not judged.
